The excerpt (which is the famous opening paragraph of Thomas Mann's *Death in Venice*) follows a completely logical and unified progression. It begins with the protagonist's internal state—his mental exhaustion from his morning's writing—which directly motivates his action to take a walk in the afternoon. The narrative then smoothly tracks his physical journey through Munich, moving from the crowded park to quieter paths as the day progresses and his physical fatigue sets in. Finally, the approaching storm and his tiredness logically lead him to wait for the tram at the cemetery. Furthermore, the external atmosphere (the "threatening" year, the oppressive heat of the "false summer," the gathering storm, and the silent graveyard) seamlessly mirrors and reinforces his internal exhaustion and sets a unified, foreboding tone for the narrative.
